UPGRADED TO P1 by cold review (2026-09-01 at 788c0c21f; review artifacts
in session scratchpad rev107/: protoC.patch, protoE.patch, probes/,
sweeps). THE PROOF THE DEFECT IS LIVE-BUT-ARMED:

(1) probes/halt.fz (10 lines): Enumerable.reduce(1..5, {:cont,0}, halt-
at-3 reducer) -- base FIFO and LIFO both print {:halted,3}; under a
LEGAL arm order that puts the {:cont,int}-narrow arm first it prints
{:done,3}. The kdt.104 defect verbatim, still constructible.
(2) behavior/enum_predicate_search AND behavior/enum_map_family:
reversing each runtime-indistinguishable arm group (a legal order) makes
native ABORT (exit 134) in _fz_list_head_int_ref: the 3-arm
List.reduce_while_cont/3 group has arms over [:false|:true] /
[int|:ok|:true] / [int] whose bodies use INCOMPATIBLE element accessors;
all three project to ONE runtime predicate (list shapes = Empty/NonEmpty
only). Base is green only because arrival order puts an atom-list arm
first. Interp survives (dynamic tags); native aborts -- also a
three-path-parity hazard.

CENSUS (re-measured): 17 indistinguishable groups / 10 fixtures =
12 no-question (closure identity; arms 1..n provably unreachable -- the
plan emits ZERO tests; see the dead-specialization ticket) + 5
list-element (the abort class) + 0 tuple-payload in fixtures (halt.fz's
class lives in Range.reduce_cont/6-step/6, reachable from source).

OPTION (C) -- canonical arm order -- PROTOTYPED AND REFUTED, do not
re-propose: 4 lib failures incl. 2 wrong answers ({:done,3} where
{:halted,3}); ZERO confluence gained (enum_map_family 1504->1504 diff
lines -- 570 of them under `selection`, fz-kdt.108's site, cross-class
block movement; 00277 948->948, a demand delta upstream of dispatch);
for 12/17 groups the observable surfaces are byte-identical so the
'canonical' choice would rest on types/order.rs's documented mint-order
residual; and the corpus stdout sweep is PROVABLY INSUFFICIENT as a gate
(C passed it while shipping the miscompile -- the failures live in
drive_test inline fixtures only).

THE CURE, three sequenced steps (reviewer-specified):
- Step 1 = fz-kdt.118 (drop rule judges containment on OBSERVABLE
  surfaces; ~8-line protoE measured green; soundness question named
  there).
- Step 2 = fz-kdt.119 (predicate learns per-position atom tags in
  fixed-arity tuples; dissolves the tuple class at the predicate).
- Step 3 = THIS ticket's core, after 118+119: the 5 list-element groups.
  No arm covers another; no O(1) predicate separates them ([] ties every
  list arm; heterogeneous lists defeat first-element probes); bodies are
  physically incompatible. Sound options: (A) real element
  discrimination (O(n), price it), (B) do not mint indistinguishable
  siblings (joins post-106 genuine correlation width, forces lanes
  wider -- an epic), or the honest interim: a plan whose alternatives
  are runtime-indistinguishable AND uncovered is UNREPRESENTABLE --
  emit a compile-time diagnostic instead of silently order-decided
  routing (turns a latent abort into a fact; price the corpus fallout:
  it fires on 5 groups / 2-4 fixtures today).

PERMANENT GATES REQUIRED (with step 3): extend
compiler2_dispatch_offers_no_runtime_indistinguishable_arm from its 2
fixtures to the census 10 (currently scoped precisely because those two
carry none -- it is red on the census today); plus an env-gated
arm-REVERSAL stress asserting corpus stdout invariance (the only gate
that catches this class; protoE.patch carries the knob). Do NOT add a
canonical-order gate.

FIFO/LIFO NOTE: behavior never flips between today's two schedules
(0/579 both ways) -- the miscompiling orders are legal-but-unproduced.
That is exactly kdt.104's situation and why this is P1 not P3.
Related: fz-kdt.108 owns enum_map_family's canon gap (rewritten);
00277's delta is kdt.106-class blocked by closure positions (see the
absorption-gaps ticket); dead_closure_capture_empty_list has a THIRD
residue class (return-precision, own ticket).

DIG MEASUREMENTS (2026-09-01 at 788c0c21f, pre-design; proposal
kdt107-proposal.md in session scratchpad, cold review in flight):

(1) The previously-unmeasured FIFO/LIFO evidence: BEHAVIOR NEVER FLIPS.
All four shape-(2) fixtures stdout-identical FIFO vs LIFO on interp AND
JIT. The defect is latent -- arm order is semantics in principle; the
corpus's values never disagree with the schedule's choice.

(2) Post-fz-kdt.106 the ENTIRE remaining schedule-visible artifact
surface is two of this ticket's fixtures:
- enum_map_family: key sets IDENTICAL (151==151), canon differs 1,170
  lines (normalized-multiset residual 390): at the SAME dispatch node
  FIFO tests type(list(binary)) where LIFO tests type(list(int)),
  repeated ~45x. Both questions project to the SAME runtime predicate
  (runtime_type_predicate_list_shapes records Empty/NonEmpty only,
  types/mod.rs:2265) -- the match edge's arm is fiat, schedule-authored.
- 00277: 180 vs 181 execs; key delta = LIFO mints dbg/fz_dbg_value
  [empty_list()] where FIFO mints Range.reduce/5[...,{:cont,
  empty_list()},...] -- a DEMAND divergence upstream of dispatch (not
  kdt.106's chain class), plus 562 canon lines downstream.

(3) Design space priced in the proposal: (A) predicate strengthening
(O(n) list checks; O(1) first-element probe unsound for heterogeneous +
answers nothing for []); (B) don't-mint-indistinguishable-siblings (an
epic: joins genuine post-106 correlation width, forces lanes wider --
the fz-y6w/qwf trade reversed); (C) HEADLINE: canonically order
runtime-indistinguishable alternatives by cmp_ty on surfaces --
schedule-confluence now, deterministic fiat instead of lucky fiat,
(A)/(B) stay this ticket's long-term question on a stable base.

Step 1 (fz-kdt.118) built. Measurements that move this ticket's own numbers:

- The 17-group census, re-measured base vs head through the artifact gate
  helper: indistinguishable arm PAIRS 27 -> 22. 0 of the 12 closure-identity
  groups move (mutual containment; a unit test pins that boundary). 2 of the 5
  list-element groups shed their `list(int)` member -- observably contained in
  its `list(int | :ok | :true)` sibling, and shielded at base only by the
  reducer's closure literal.
- The arm-reversal sweep this ticket demanded now exists
  (FZ_STRESS_REVERSE_DISPATCH_ARMS, plus the lib gate
  `compiler2_dispatch_answers_the_same_under_a_reversed_arm_order`). Census
  movers under reversal: 3 -> 1. enum_predicate_search STOPS aborting, because
  the arm fz-kdt.118 drops is the incompatible-accessor one. enum_map_family
  remains (exit 134 in fz_list_head_int_ref) and is this ticket's step 3.

NEW EVIDENCE FOR STEP 3, and it changes the framing: the residue is not a
latent hazard, it is a LIVE WRONG ANSWER at 788c0c21f. See fz-kdt.125:

  defmodule Pipeline do
    fn apply_twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: apply_twice(f, x)
  end
  fn main() do
    dbg(Pipeline.run(fn (n) -> n + 1 end, 10))
    dbg(Pipeline.run(fn (n) -> n * 3 end, 10))
  end

prints 12 then 12 for 12 then 90, on run + interp + AOT. One forwarding hop is
the whole recipe -- no protocol, no annotation, no stdlib. The invoker
specializes on the closure literal and GROUNDS A DIRECT CALL to it, so the
sibling's lambda never runs; with captures it reads the wrong capture record
and aborts. This is the "12 no-question closure-identity groups" line of the
census with the grounding path attached, and it means step 3's option list must
cover it: keeping both arms is not a safety net here, it is a plan in which
arm 1 is dead code.

It also settles a question step 3 would otherwise have to ask: a
"do not drop when the callable position is grounded" carve-out changes no
answer. Dropping a runtime-indistinguishable arm never changes a routing, since
the plan asks no question that separates the group -- Pipeline.run's pair is
mutual containment, nothing is dropped either way, and it miscompiles anyway.
The cure has to be upstream: either the callsite must not offer arms it cannot
separate, or a body specialized on a closure literal must not ground a direct
call to it unless every caller proves that literal is what arrives.

F5 note from the fz-kdt.118 refutation (optional fold, deferred to this ticket's step-3 touch of callsite_dispatch.rs): reverse_indistinguishable_groups recomputes runtime_dispatch_inputs + runtime_type_predicate and re-derives which-arms-ask-one-question -- the same grouping DispatchAlternative::runtime_indistinguishable derives twenty lines later. Two spellings of the one idea this ticket turns on; fold into a shared question_groups(types, targets) helper when this file is next opened.

STEP 3 RETARGETED by the fz-kdt.125 cold review (2026-09-01): the closure-identity half of this ticket's census is DISCHARGED by fz-kdt.125's predicate axis (13/13 no-question groups separable by fn id alone -- the arms become live, fz-kdt.123 retargeted accordingly). What remains THIS ticket's: the 5 list-element groups (bodies with incompatible element accessors, no O(1) predicate; enum_map_family's arm-reversal abort is the live evidence, named in the fz-kdt.118 stress-gate doc). The 'unrepresentable plan' diagnostic is PROMOTED from interim option to REQUIRED backstop (it also owns fz-kdt.127's same-fn-id residue). Dependency now: blocked by 119 + 125; 118 closed.

Step 3's closure-identity half is DISCHARGED by fz-kdt.125 (2026-09-01), and the
census numbers move:

- no-question dispatch groups 13 -> 6, fixtures 9 -> 5. All six survivors are

  by fn id" was a census-helper artifact (it counted closure names appearing in

- `compiler2_dispatch_offers_no_runtime_indistinguishable_arm` widened from 2

- The measured residue is pinned by a new sibling gate,
  `compiler2_runtime_indistinguishable_arm_residue_stays_pinned`: 00231 1,
  00277 5, 00281 1, enum_map_family 3, opaque_fn_value_join 1,
  repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 1. Two owners: the same-fn-id shape

- ARM_ORDER_CENSUS is now 13 fixtures; the reversal stress gate is green.

NEW, and it is this ticket's own subject read from the other side: making the
arms live gives the SCHEDULE something new to decide. fz-kdt.129 records it --
the corpus's FIFO-vs-LIFO backend-dump population goes 3 -> 4, and the fourth is
enum_predicate_search, a lens. The 28 moved lines are two arms of one dispatch
swapping positions; they are DISTINGUISHABLE and nested, so order costs
precision rather than meaning (corpus stdout is byte-identical either way), but
the artifact is no longer schedule-confluent there. fz-kdt.129 names
`Order::Specificity` over the observable containment order as the candidate,
with the explicit carve-out that indistinguishable groups keep arrival order --
this ticket's option (C) stays refuted.

STEP 3 SPEC SETTLED by cold review with full prototype (2026-09-01 at
dd97b2df2; kdt107s3-proto.patch + prototype-src in session scratchpad;
9 files ~250 lines, all three lowerings built and measured):

THE DESIGN: ListShapes { shapes, heads: Vec<RuntimeTypePredicate>,
exact } beside the set (TupleShapes treatment); one head per
cons-admitting clause; multi-positive-sig or negated clauses degrade
the whole axis to shape_only. Runtime test = cons check + ONE head
load + the landed per-position machinery (O(1), both doors already
import the accessor).

THE LAW (my proposal's erasing rule REFUTED by prototype -- it seated
[int] ahead of [int|:ok] and re-created the abort, strictly worse than
base's drop): the head test is a ONE-SIDED FILTER -- exact on
REJECTION (uniform element type: a head outside the question proves
the value outside the surface), erasing on ACCEPTANCE (proves nothing
about the tail). Lattice form: NonEmpty vs NonEmpty overlap => ERASING
wherever heads overlap AT ALL (disjoint heads are the only claimable
separation); Empty non-erasing ([] is one value carrying nothing);
either inexact => erasing.

MEASURED OUTCOMES (corrected rule): the enum_map_family reversal ABORT
DIES (rc 134->0, both schedules; via A/C head disjointness);
indistinguishable residue 12->6, ALL six = fz-kdt.127's same-fn-id
shape (the list-element half of this ticket's census fully
discharged); 19-escape census honestly 19->2 after correcting the
instrument (blind_escapes triggers on predicate EQUALITY, not the
overlaps_on_an_erasing_axis relation production uses -- base is 19
under both, so the correction is independently verifiable); the two
survivors are enum_predicate_search's A/B pairs = fz-kdt.131 facet 3,
arrival-kept and PINNED (not pretended fixed); 584x2-door corpus
0 movers; +0.7-9.3% native code, mostly the UN-DROPPED narrow arms
(group-splitting loses fz-kdt.118's drop -- own ticket); [] ties are
a non-issue (measured); heterogeneous lists not-worse (abort at
element >=2 instead of 1, never preferring a narrow body over a
covering one). F2/tripwire-268 claims were MISATTRIBUTED: those are
fz-kdt.138's (one line, 132-blocked, orthogonal); 107.3 does NOT fix
F2 and is NOT blocked by 132 (measured green on take_drop both
doors).

BUILD ORDER: instrument tickets FIRST (reversal-stress-all-arms +
blind_escapes correction -- Stage 2's own green depends on them),
then Stage 2 = the 13-item spec in the review report (one commit,
three lowerings, tuple_arities_at_every_depth MUST recurse through
heads -- without it interp/JIT disagree, prototype-proven).

fz-kdt.141's permutation stress landed; step 3's evidence base is four fixtures wide now, not one.

The reversal knob this replaces could perturb ONE list seat at head (fz-kdt.118's close: 'arm-reversal movers 3->1, enum_map_family remains'). A seeded arm permutation perturbs 27 fixtures' artifacts where reversal perturbs 8, and it makes FOUR fixtures abort natively, all with one signature -- _fz_list_head_int_ref, a list of atoms read as a list of ints -- and all in this ticket's step-3 class:

  enum_map_family              arms:reverse, arms:6
  00277_enum_tier0_fixture     arms:1 .. arms:5
  dispatch_seat_element_blind  every arm seed
  enum_predicate_search        arms:6

Three of the four were unreachable by the reversal. dispatch_seat_element_blind is fz-kdt.129's own reproducer, and its native abort under a legal arrival order is the cleanest statement of this ticket to date: the fixture prints the right answers ONLY because arrival seats the atom arm first.

JIT and AOT agree fixture for fixture (AOT checked over both censuses); the interpreter is invariant everywhere -- 0 movers over 584 fixtures x 19 settings -- so this stays a three-path-parity hazard exactly as the ticket says.

None of these is a new defect: all four are this ticket's declared population. What changed is that the instrument gating step 3 is now honest -- your prerequisite (1), 'the one gate that ever caught the list-element abort class cannot perturb a single list seat', is retired. Recipe and numbers are in .agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md, section 'The two free orders, and the stress that moves them'.

title: P1: runtime-indistinguishable dispatch arms are a latent miscompile, not a fiat -- arrival order is the only thing between the corpus and a wrong answer
